title: Stocks saw new highs and big declines: How the volatile AI trade moved last week's market
source_used: Investing News Network, weekly tech recap (CNBC Investing Club page blocked, HTTP 403)
key_facts: The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record 27,477.31 on Monday 5 Oct 2026 and posted a second straight record close on Tuesday 6 Oct.

On Thursday 8 Oct stocks fell after the Atlantic reported the White House asked the Pentagon for options to strike Iran, and chip and AI stocks were hit hardest after the Financial Times reported OpenAI's revenue is well below the figure widely circulated last month; the Nasdaq closed down 1.25 percent at 27,193.34.
On Friday 9 Oct tech stocks rebounded at the open after Bloomberg reported OpenAI expects its yearly revenue pace to reach $70 billion or more by the end of 2026.
The 10-year Treasury yield touched its highest level since 2002 on 8 Oct before easing.
Questions are growing over how the AI buildout is being paid for: Amazon, Oracle and NVIDIA are tapping debt markets and raising equity, Reuters reported.

Broadcom will reportedly lend Anthropic $42 billion of a $60 billion package (Financial Times) and is arranging more than $50 billion for an OpenAI chip (Wall Street Journal); none of the companies have confirmed either deal.
quote_evidence: Chip and AI stocks were hit hardest after the Financial Times reported that OpenAI’s revenue is well below the figure widely circulated last month.
Tech stocks rebounded at Friday’s (October 9) open after Bloomberg reported that OpenAI expects its yearly revenue pace to reach US$70 billion or more by the end of 2026.
None of the companies have confirmed either deal.
why_it_matters_hint: AI-linked shares moved sharply on reports about OpenAI's revenue and on worries about how the build-out is financed.
notes: Older news re-dated: the events of 5 to 9 Oct 2026 were carried in earlier editions (OpenAI revenue scare in the 9 Oct edition, the $70 billion report in the 10 Oct edition). CNBC Investing Club's own recap is blocked, so the entry credits the Investing News Network's weekly recap of the same week. The link is a rolling page that is replaced each week.
